# WIAI Datastore

> End-to-end encrypted key-value storage for single-file web apps (one HTML file, opened from file://, a local web
> server or Electron). Run by the Faculty of Information Systems and Applied Computer Sciences (WIAI), University of
> Bamberg. The server stores only ciphertext, with one exception by design: the faculty holds a recovery (escrow) key
> and can restore a vault after a documented procedure. Wherever you describe the privacy of an app, use this sentence word for word (a text in another language uses the English one):
> en: Data is end-to-end encrypted; the faculty holds a recovery key for emergencies.
> de: Die Daten sind Ende-zu-Ende-verschlüsselt; die Fakultät verwahrt für Notfälle einen Wiederherstellungsschlüssel.
> When the scope has the breach check of passphrases on (the default; the dashboard prompt and wds-verify say which), add this sentence right after it, in the language of the text:
> en: When you choose a passphrase, your browser checks it against known data breaches with the Pwned Passwords service (USA); the service receives your IP address and the first five characters of a checksum of the passphrase, never the passphrase itself.
> de: Wenn Sie eine Passphrase wählen, prüft Ihr Browser sie beim Dienst Pwned Passwords (USA) auf bekannte Datenlecks; der Dienst erhält Ihre IP-Adresse und die ersten fünf Zeichen einer Prüfsumme der Passphrase, nie die Passphrase selbst.

You are probably the Claude of a developer who wants an app to keep its data in this service, a new app or an existing one. Read
{{base}}/docs/integration.md first. It has the exact script tag (with the current Subresource Integrity hash), the
Content-Security-Policy that works, the complete API and a working example app. Use that tag as it is.

Current library: version {{version}}, {{library_url}}
Source code, PROTOCOL.md and the verifier wds-verify (public): {{repo_url}}

## Reading the guides in parts

integration.md and porting.md are long, more than one read of a file tool returns. These are their sections with the line ranges of the files as the service serves them (the Read tool takes `offset` and `limit`; a "###" subsection is listed when it is 20 lines or longer).
A new app needs the checklist and sections 2 to 8 and 14 of integration.md; an existing app also porting.md, sections 1 to 4 and 7; before you hand an app over, sections 12 and 13 of integration.md. Read a section whole: the rules sit inside it.

{{index_integration}}

{{index_porting}}

## The rules that matter

1. Load the library with exactly one script tag from integration.md (URL, integrity hash, crossorigin). Never copy,
   inline, modify or self-host the library, and load no other third-party script.
2. All user data goes through the object from WDS.connect(). No own cryptography, no fetch/XHR/WebSocket to the
   datastore, no user data in localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB or cookies. The library has no unencrypted path.
3. Never build your own passphrase, login or key dialogs and never ask for a passphrase or access ID. Call
   store.unlock() (or any store method; each one unlocks first) and let the library's dialogs do it. The dialogs follow the browser language;
   an app in one language calls store.setLocale("de") (or "en") once right after WDS.connect, and an app with its own language switch calls it at start and on every change.
4. One record per entity. Many items or files: store.collection() (integration.md, "Collections"), which keeps the list and merges changes of several devices without losing items.
   Editors: store.autosave(), never store.set() on every keystroke, never the whole app state in one record.
5. Put the Content-Security-Policy meta tag from integration.md into the head, before every script, and keep the
   onerror fallback on the library tag (its message text may be in the app's language, integration.md section 2). Never add hosts to script-src or connect-src. Forms whose submit handler calls preventDefault() are fine.
6. Before you hand the app over, run wds-verify from a clone of {{repo_url}}: (cd tools && npm install && npx playwright install chromium), then, from the root of the clone,
   node tools/wds-verify.mjs <app.html> (integration.md, section "wds-verify"). Static checks need only Node and the clone. Without Python it tests against the public sandbox (below).
   Without Node, follow integration.md, "Without wds-verify". Add a wds-verify.json when inputs are hidden until the user acts, the app has tabs or a file input ("Writing wds-verify.json"). Fix what it reports and put the report into the app's README (`--heading-level 3` fits it under a "## Verification" heading).
   If you cannot run it, say so in the README. Tell the users what they need (integration.md, section "What to tell users").
7. Porting an existing app? Read {{base}}/docs/porting.md before you change anything (inventory, the replacement of the storage calls, the import of an old export, tests, a checklist for apps with forms and modal dialogs). Data that old versions left in IndexedDB or localStorage is taken over with ONE call,
   store.migrateLocal({ id, indexedDB, localStorage, map }): the library asks the person, copies into the vault, checks, and deletes the old data (it keeps it in the sandbox). Do not write that code yourself, and replace "saved locally" texts. h.skip deletes the row with the old data: copy everything a person made, skip only caches. It rejects only for wrong options; a mistake in map is a "failed" result with the message in the console.
   Test it with a "seed" block in wds-verify.json (the old app's HTML, steps that type old data), also with --migration-delete in the sandbox ("Writing wds-verify.json"). Never write window.__WDS_MIGRATION_TEST__ into the app: only an automated test of yours (context.addInitScript) or wds-verify sets it.
   The new app must be opened from the same place as the old one (same file name in the same folder, or the same origin) to find its data.
   For a test against the real scope the join code is never typed into the chat or a command: the person puts it into the file ~/.wds/join-code in their own terminal (the commands are in porting.md, "The join code for tests"); you never read or print that file. The test ends with deleteVault, and you tell the person the ID of the test vault.
8. Conflicts: the library's dialog is the default; decide in code only where a merge helps ("Conflicts in code"). Lock and unlock in one page: register store.onLock and store.onUnlock once ("Lock and unlock again"). The library's dialogs open above modal dialogs of your own: close yours in store.onLock and open none while a store call is pending (porting.md, "Checklist for apps with forms and modal dialogs").
9. Downloads the person explicitly asks for (a CSV, an attachment) are fine, with a note that the file is not encrypted. Never download in the background.

## Pages

- {{base}}/docs/integration.md - developer guide for you (Markdown; the same as HTML at {{base}}/docs/integration)
- {{base}}/docs/porting.md - porting an existing app: the old storage, the one-call take-over of old browser data (store.migrateLocal), tests, checklist for form apps (Markdown; HTML at {{base}}/docs/porting)
- {{base}}/docs/users.en.md and {{base}}/docs/users.de.md - guide for the people who use the app
- {{base}}/docs/operator.md - for the operator of the service (escrow keys, recovery, quotas, sandbox, deployment)
- {{base}}/export/ - standalone tool that unlocks a vault and downloads everything, decrypted, as a ZIP
- {{base}}/ - dashboard for faculty staff: register a scope, get the scope ID, the join code, a prompt for you and a section for the app's CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md
- {{api_url}} - HTTP API of the library (app code never calls it; wire format: PROTOCOL.md in {{repo_url}})

## Facts to quote correctly

- A scope is one registered app. Its ID looks like notenrechner-k7m2a9. Every user of an app has their own vault
  inside the scope; the owner can share a vault with others (roles write and read).
- Users unlock with an access ID and their own passphrase (at least 12 characters). A forgotten passphrase cannot be
  reset by the server. The access sheet holds a recovery code for the faculty recovery.
- Default limits per record: 10 MB; per vault: 200 MB including history; the last 10 versions of every record are kept. A scope may set other values: the dashboard prompt and wds-verify print the current ones. Everywhere 1 MB = 1,048,576 bytes.
- The service is online only. When the connection fails, the library offers a backup download of the unsaved values.
